title: SIG questionnaire walkthrough - Argentum Bank
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Argentum Bank through the SIG questionnaire. Focus areas were SOC 2 certification timing, ISO artifacts, RBAC/SSO integration, audit log retention and access, encryption and KMS key ownership, and evidence packaging for VRQ. Agreed next steps include sharing SOC 2 report, ISO 27001 cert, specific audit log screenshots, and a completed SIG spreadsheet. Follow-up demo for private deployment options if needed.
next_steps: Emily to share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate (link) - by 2026-06-26
Daniel to provide screenshots of audit log UI and sample retention settings - by 2026-06-29
Emily to upload completed SIG spreadsheet with referenced evidence links - by 2026-06-26
Schedule follow-up call for deeper private deployment / VPC discussion - target 2026-07-02
action_items: Emily Park - Share SOC 2 report and ISO cert (attach redacted PDFs) - due 2026-06-26
Daniel Cho - Export audit log screenshots + sample RBAC settings - due 2026-06-29
Aisha Rahman - Confirm internal VRQ reviewers and timeline - due 2026-06-28
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Emily Park (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Sarah Martinez (CISO, Argentum), Liam O'Neill (InfoSec Manager, Argentum), Aisha Rahman (Procurement, Argentum)
transcript:
[00:00] Emily: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, I'm Emily from Redwood, Daniel's with me.
[00:08] Daniel: Hey all.
[00:10] Sarah: Hey, Sarah here.
[00:12] Liam: Liam on the line.
[00:14] Aisha: Aisha here.
[00:16] Emily: Great. The purpose today is a walkthrough of the SIG / security questionnaire and to surface any evidence requests you have. We'll go section by section, call out what we can share, and flag anything that needs a follow up. Sound good?
[00:28] Sarah: Yes that's right. We try to get all the evidence packaged for our vendor risk team. We're mostly focused on SOC 2 and data residency.
[00:36] Emily: Understood. Quick housekeeping: we'll keep this to 45, and we'll note action items. Daniel, do you want to kick off on infrastructure and encryption?
[00:44] Daniel: Sure. So Redwood's runtime is deployed in a few different modes — hosted API, dedicated pools, and private VPC. For hosted, we run on major cloud providers, we can provide regionality for data residency — so EU, US, APAC when available. For dedicated we reserve GPU capacity and for private we can install a customer-managed control plane in their VPC or on-prem.
[01:10] Liam: Quick Q — for private deploys, do you still manage keys or do we? Key ownership is important for us.
[01:16] Daniel: For private deployment you can bring your own keys and integrate with your KMS or HSM. For hosted we offer envelope encryption; we manage service-side keys but offer KMS integrations and you can request customer-managed keys with additional contractual terms.
[01:30] Sarah: And what about audit logs? Our vendor team needs proof of tamper-evident logs and retention.
[01:36] Daniel: We provide structured audit logs for control-plane actions and per-request logs for inference calls. Logs are immutable in storage and we can export to your SIEM via streaming (S3, PubSub, etc.). Retention default is 90 days for hosted but can be extended for Dedicated/Private. We'll attach screenshots of the audit console.
[01:56] Aisha: Any SOC 2 that we can attach?
[01:58] Emily: Yes we have a SOC 2 Type II report as of Q1 2026. We'll send the redacted PDF. We also have ISO 27001 cert in place; docs will be provided.
[02:10] Liam: In the SIG spreadsheet there's a question about RBAC and SSO — do you support SAML/Okta?
[02:16] Daniel: Yes, we support SAML-based SSO and SCIM user provisioning; RBAC is role-based with fine-grained roles across the console and API keys. For Dedicated/Private you get stronger separation — network controls plus RBAC.
[02:30] Sarah: Do you log admin actions? We need change management audit trail.
[02:34] Daniel: Yes, admin actions are logged with actor, timestamp, and metadata. We can provide sample log lines to show the fields.
[02:42] Emily: On data residency, Argenta... Argentum sorry, where's your main concern? EU data residency for EU customers?
[02:52] Sarah: Correct. We need to demonstrate any EU customer data never leaves region.
[02:56] Daniel: For hosted, we can pin deployments to EU regions and all transient KV/cache and logs remain in-region when pinned. For additional guarantees we recommend Dedicated in-region or Private deployment inside your VPC.
[03:12] Liam: There's also a question about encryption in transit and at rest.
[03:16] Daniel: We use TLS 1.2/1.3 for in transit, and encrypt at rest with AES-256. For KMS, we integrate with cloud KMS and support customer-supplied keys in private deployments. Note — sometimes the transcript generator writes K M S as separate letters in the doc.
[03:34] Sarah: (laughs) noted.
[03:36] Aisha: For evidence, our vendor team wants screenshots and maybe extracts — not full logs.
[03:40] Emily: We'll provide redacted examples and metadata mapping to SIG control IDs.
[03:44] Liam: Any third-party pen test results?
[03:46] Daniel: We do yearly third-party penetration tests; we can provide exec summary and remediation notes, redacted for customer consumption.
[03:54] Sarah: On compliance, a few SIG items ask about subcontractors and subprocessors. What's your current list?
[03:59] Emily: We can send our current vendor/subprocessor list; it's maintained by security. Includes major cloud providers and monitoring vendors — we'll provide the redacted list.
[04:10] Emily: Okay let's open the SIG sheet — (screen share noise) — starting with A. Physical and Environmental controls, most of these map to our CSPs, we mark as shared responsibility.
[04:26] Speaker 1: There's a question on encryption key lifecycle management — do you rotate keys regularly?
[04:32] Daniel: Yes, for customer-managed we recommend rotation policies; for our managed keys we rotate according to industry best practices and can provide rotation logs.
[04:40] [04:40] Sarah: There's a section on incident response — can you describe your IR process and SLA for breach notification?
[04:47] Emily: We have an incident response plan, we've tabletop annually, and typical notification SLA is 72 hours for confirmed breaches plus ongoing updates. For customers with contractual needs we can negotiate specific timelines.
[04:58] Liam: Do you have a dedicated security contact for urgent incidents?
[05:02] Emily: Yes, we have a 24/7 on-call rotation in security and a primary security email and pager routing for critical incidents.
[05:10] Aisha: Procurement asks for insurance details — cyber policy and limits.
[05:14] Emily: We carry a cyber liability policy; we'll include the certificate of insurance with limits in the pack.
[05:20] Daniel: Moving to access control sample — here's where RBAC is shown; roles include Admin, DevOps, Billing, ReadOnly. We can show how API keys are scoped and how tokens are audited.
[05:34] Liam: Are API keys rotatable by customer?
[05:36] Daniel: Yes keys can be rotated and revoked by owner or via automation.
[05:40] Sarah: On data deletion and backups — can you confirm the backup retention and deletion procedures?
[05:45] Daniel: Backups are encrypted and retained per our policy; for hosted we retain backups for 30 days by default, with longer retention options for Dedicated/Private. When a customer requests deletion we follow documented workflows to delete data from active storage and request deletion from backups in accordance with the contract — we'll attach the deletion playbook.
[06:05] Aisha: For the SIG control where it asks if any data leaves the EU, you said pinning keeps data in-region, but are there exceptions like admin access from outside?
[06:14] Daniel: Admin access can be restricted via IP allowlists and SSO settings. For full EU data residency we recommend Private deployment where control plane and logs never transit outside the region. We'll call out the exceptions in notes.
[06:30] Speaker 1: There's a question about vulnerability management cadence and patching windows.
[06:34] Daniel: We run regular vulnerability scans, monthly scans and critical patching within 48-72 hours depending on severity, and maintain a CVE tracking board. We can provide our VM policy and sample scan results.
[06:48] Sarah: Could you share the SOC 2 scope — which trust services categories are covered?
[06:53] Emily: SOC 2 Type II covers Security and Availability; we can provide scope details in the report. We're in progress to extend coverage to Confidentiality — ETA is Q3 2026, but I'll confirm.
[07:06] Liam: For SIG/CAIQ, some questions need proof artifacts like config snippets. Are you comfortable with us sharing redacted configs?
[07:12] Daniel: Yes, redacted configs and screenshots are standard. We avoid sharing private keys or secrets.
[07:18] Aisha: Procurement will want an attestation about subprocessor due diligence.
[07:22] Emily: We'll include our subprocessor onboarding checklist and attestations.
[07:26] Sarah: A few items about change management — do you have a formal change advisory board?
[07:30] Daniel: We have a change control process, CAB for major changes, and release notes tracked. We'll provide a sample change record.
[07:38] [07:38] Liam: Anything special on encryption algorithms? Some auditors ask for specifics.
[07:42] Daniel: We use AES-256-GCM at rest and TLS 1.2+/ECDHE for transit. KMS integrations use provider-managed envelopes.
[07:52] Sarah: On multi-tenancy — is there logical separation between customers in hosted mode?
[07:57] Daniel: Yes logical separation and strong namespace isolation; for customers requiring physical separation we recommend Dedicated pools.
[08:06] Emily: Let's mark the SIG items that require evidence: SOC report (attach), ISO cert (attach), audit log screenshots, RBAC config screenshot, KMS integration docs, pen test exec summary, subprocessor list. Anything else?
[08:20] Aisha: Insurance cert and COI.
[08:22] Sarah: Also a sample data deletion runbook.
[08:24] Emily: Great. We'll assemble a single zip with redacted items and a mapping to each SIG control.
[08:30] Liam: One more — the VRQ asks about disaster recovery RTO/RPO.
[08:34] Daniel: Typical RTOs vary by deployment; for Dedicated we target 4 hour RTO for core control plane incidents and RPO is often minutes given replication. We'll include the DR runbook excerpt with anonymized timings.
[08:48] Sarah: For encryption key escrow — any mechanism?
[08:52] Daniel: For customer-managed keys you control the key material, escrow is customer responsibility; we don't hold keys unless contracted and then it's under strict controls.
[09:03] Aisha: How will you deliver the evidence? Secure upload?
[09:06] Emily: We'll upload to a secure share (SFTP or secure portal) and provide time-limited links. We'll also add references in the SIG sheet.
[09:16] [09:16] Sarah: Do you have logs for administrative privilege elevation? We need proof of approval flows.
[09:22] Daniel: Yes, privilege elevation requests and approvals are recorded. We can pull audit trails showing requestor, approver, and timestamps.
[09:30] Liam: A quick note on deployment — if we go Dedicated in-region, will that give us SLA credits for downtime?
[09:36] Emily: Dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime and we can include penalty/credits in contracts. We'll follow up with legal on the SLA wording if you want specifics.
[09:48] Sarah: Are there any known open issues with your SOC report or outstanding exceptions?
[09:52] Emily: No material exceptions right now. We'll include the management response section if any small items exist.
[09:58] Daniel: One minor callout — sometimes the auto transcript muddles product names like "Redwood Dedicated" -> "red wood dedicated" in the docs; ignore that.
[10:08] Aisha: (laughs) noted.
[10:10] Emily: Okay, next section — monitoring and alerting.
[10:14] Daniel: We provide monitoring metrics, alerting integrations (PagerDuty, OpsGenie), and can stream telemetry to your observability stack. Alerts have defined escalation policies.
[10:26] Sarah: For the SIG question on code security, do you sign-off on secure coding standards?
[10:32] Daniel: We follow secure development lifecycle practices, code reviews, and static analysis — we can supply the SDL summary.
[10:40] Liam: For onboarding, does SSO support Just-in-Time provisioning?
[10:44] Daniel: Yes JIT through SAML/SCIM is supported.
[10:48] Emily: I want to make sure we captured action items — we'll send SOC 2, ISO cert, pen test summary, subprocessor list, audit screenshots, RBAC screenshots, KMS docs, COI, deletion runbook, DR summary. Anything else?
[11:02] Sarah: That covers it. We'll review the SIG mapping and get back with any additional asks.
[11:08] Aisha: Procurement will need the COI and a standard contract redline — expect a separate thread.
[11:14] Emily: Understood. We'll coordinate with your procurement.
[11:18] Liam: Can we get a sample SLA document?
[11:20] Emily: Yes, I'll include the generic SLA and we can iterate.
[11:24] Daniel: Final technical note — if you want to run a short benchmark for latency within EU region we can provision a dedicated pool for a proof-of-concept.
[11:34] Sarah: That may be helpful.
[11:36] Emily: We'll propose a small POC scope in the follow-up.
[11:40] Aisha: Timeline wise, if we get the artifacts by next Friday we can wrap up vendor review the following week.
[11:48] Emily: Sounds good. We'll target sending artifacts by Friday.
[11:52] Sarah: Thanks everyone.
[11:54] Emily: Thanks all — we'll follow up with links and the filled SIG spreadsheet.
[11:58] [END]
